leads.posting: About the internship You'll write and iterate the prompts that drive Avya's voice interviews question flows, follow-up logic, and how the agent evaluates what a candidate actually said. This is not prompt tinkering: a live interview is a multi-turn conversation with a real person's job on the line, and it has to hold up when things go sideways. That means designing for the edge cases as much as the happy path. What happens when a candidate goes silent mid-answer, or interrupts, or switches to Hinglish, or gives an answer nobody anticipated. You'll test prompts against real transcripts and adversarial inputs before they ship, and when something breaks in production you'll debug it to root cause figuring out whether the fix belongs in the prompt, in the pipeline, or in the data being fed to the model, and then making that fix. You'll also work directly with product on what the interview should feel like from the candidate's side. Opinions are expected, not just execution. leads.title: Rust Systems Engineer, Browser Security
leads.posting: Datamint | Rust Systems Engineer, Browser Security | Remote (Global) | Full-time | $120k–$170k + Equity | https://datamint.xyz We build high-throughput crawling and structured data extraction infra designed for AI agents and LLM pipelines. If you’ve built scrapers recently, you already know the state of the market: - Traditional proxy providers (Bright Data, Oxylabs, Smartproxy, Proxybase) give you raw IPs or massive unparsed HTML blobs, leaving you to deal with DOM bloat, token waste, and brittle parsing pipelines. - Modern tools like Firecrawl or Jina made clean Markdown extraction easy for hobby setups, but they often struggle when you throw heavy SPAs, high-concurrency jobs, or hardened anti-bot walls (Cloudflare Under-Attack / Turnstile, Kasada, DataDome) at them. - Rolling your own Playwright / Puppeteer cluster works until target sites deploy new JA4/TLS fingerprints, and your data team ends up spending 30% of their sprints fixing broken crawlers instead of shipping product. We're tackling this by combining a low-latency Rust fast-fetch engine (JA4/TLS and HTTP/2 frame emulation) with an isolated stealth browser fleet, zero-code schema validation (JSON Schema/Pydantic), and native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support. Trade-offs / where we fit: If you just need to curl a few static Wikipedia pages, a 10-line Python script is better and cheaper. But if you need reliable, structured data out of bot-defended sites without babying headless browsers, that's what we do. We're looking for: 1. Rust Systems Engineer: High-concurrency network I/O, Axum/Tokio, TLS/BoringSSL fingerprinting, proxy routing matrices, and low-latency data pipelines. 2. Browser Security Engineer: Deep familiarity with browser internals (Firefox/Chromium source), canvas/WebGL/audio fingerprint evasion, CDP/WebDriver stealth, and familarity with anti-bot defenses. Our stack: Rust, Next.js 16/React 19, TypeScript, hardened Firefox/dwx_crawler, Linux/Xvfb, SQLite WAL/Postgres. If interested, shoo

[https://datamint.xyz/] datamint: clean web data for AI agents Crawling infrastructure for AI agents Clean, typed data from the sites that block everyone else. datamint crawls your hardest targets and returns LLM-ready Markdown or schema-validated JSON in a single call. No proxy pools to maintain, no parsers to re-fix every sprint. Start free See how it works 1,000 free credits every month · No card required · Blocked requests cost nothing mint.sh $ curl -X POST https://api.datamint.xyz/v1/mint \ -H "Authorization: Bearer mint_live_xxx" \ -d ' { "url" : "https://example.com/item/123" , "schema" : "ecommerce_item" , "js" : true } ' response 200 { "title" : "Aeron Chair, Graphite" , "price" : 1795.00 , "sku" : "HM-AER-GRA" , "availability" : "in_stock" , "confidence" : 0.98 } 1,000 credits / month Free every month, not a one-off trial. No card to start Sign up and make requests without a sales call. On delivery only A blocked request that returns nothing costs nothing. Public data only No paywalls, no authenticated sessions, ever. What you get back Your scraper gets a DOM. You get a record. Bot-defended pages return the same thing to everyone: markup built for a browser, wrapped in a challenge. Stripping that into something a model can read is the part that keeps breaking. raw response 403 · challenged
Checking your browser…
datamint response 200 · minted { "title" : "Aeron Chair, Graphite" , "price" : 1795.00 , "currency" : "USD" , "sku" : "HM-AER-GRA" , "availability" : "in_stock" , "_mint_meta" : { "confidence" : 0.98 , "minted_at" : "2026-09-13T07:45:02Z" } } Same shape, every run Fields are validated against your schema before the response leaves. A miss is a flagged request, never a silent null. Confidence included Every object carries a score. Below 0.80 the request reroutes through fallback rather than returning holes. Provenance attached Capture timestamp and source URL travel with the record, so any value can be traced to the page state that produced it. How it works Router first, browser last. Most requests never touch a headless browser, which is why the per-page cost stays where it is. Escalation is automatic and only goes as far as the target forces it. 01 Point at a URL One POST with the target and, optionally, the shape you want back. Nothing to install, no proxy pool to configure, no browser to keep alive. 02 We pick the cheapest route that works A static TLS-spoofed fetch first. A headless browser only if the page needs JavaScript. Residential routing only if the target rejects everything else. The route is remembered per target. 03 Get back something you can use Clean Markdown for a model to read, or JSON validated against your schema. Either way it arrives with a confidence score and provenance attached. A request that cannot be served costs nothing. You are billed for pages that come back with usable data, not for attempts. Ingestion Four ways in. One normalized shape out. Every surface runs the same normalization pipeline, so data arriving by synchronous call and data arriving by overnight batch crawl have identical structure. POST /v1/mint 800ms–2.5s Synchronous extract Single-page fetch with rendering options and an extraction schema. Returns cleaned Markdown or validated JSON in under 2.5s. View documentation → POST /v1/crawl Async Asynchronous deep crawl Traverses subdomains or path patterns with breadth and depth controls, regex filtering, deduplication, and automatic sitemap discovery. Delivers by webhook or cloud storage dump. View documentation → POST /v1/extract Schema-driven Zero-code schema extraction Supply a JSON Schema or Pydantic model. leads.posting: Tahoma AI | tahoma.io | Austin, TX or Seattle, WA (ONSITE optional) | REMOTE (US) | Full-time | Founding Engineer Tahoma builds AI agents that automate healthcare Revenue Cycle Management (RCM): eligibility, claim status, claim submission, denials, and payment posting. We're live in production with paying enterprise customers. Our agents operate payer portals behind MFA, green-screen terminals over SSH, and Windows desktop software, where some actions are irreversible. They run on a deterministic orchestration layer we built in-house, with model calls as bounded steps, not the control loop. Stack: TypeScript/Node.js, Playwright, computer-use agents, Claude, Postgres, Azure, K8s. You'll get to own the core platform end to end and make the real architecture calls: resilience to portal changes, exactly-once guarantees, observability, and cost per run. Team: Founder from AWS, the former UnitedHealthcare CIO, advisors from Microsoft Research and Shopify's AI team, and a remote engineering team in-flight. Please write us at careers@tahoma.io with your resume and one thing you've shipped. You can see more at https://www.tahoma.io/careers Thanks!
